subject: Inquiry: transaction ACK mismatch causing retry amplification — SLA remedy and postmortem
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@silvercart.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@silvercart.com
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 03:45:00 +0000
Subject: High retry volume after token endpoint 503s (observed 03:12–03:35 UTC)

Hi Rachel —

We saw a surge of retry attempts on our checkout traffic this morning that coincided with 503 responses from your tokenization endpoint (POST /v2/tokens). Our telemetry shows our clients retried aggressively and we ended up with a retry amplification that lasted ~23 minutes (03:12–03:35 UTC). This caused elevated latency and some transaction duplicates for us.

Attached are the raw traces and a CSV with the timeline and error codes. Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood observed a regional handoff or controller restart around that window
- Whether this meets the SLA definition for "unavailability" or "severe degradation" and what the remedy process is

We'd like to request a formal verification of the downtime window and a postmortem (we need that for our compliance team). Also: given the client-side retry amplification, would Redwood consider a proportional credit for the impacted volume?

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Patel
Head of Platform Ops, SilverCart
attachments: silvercart-raw-traces-20271102.tar.gz, 500-spike-timeline.csv

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@silvercart.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 04:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: High retry volume after token endpoint 503s (observed 03:12–03:35 UTC)

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the traces. We're pulling telemetry now. Initial note: our edge autoscaler logged multiple worker evictions in us-west-2 at ~03:11 UTC followed by a small control-plane topology change at ~03:14 UTC. That matches the timing you observed.

To make sure we evaluate correctly for SLA eligibility, please confirm whether your affected client requests were hitting our tokenization-hostname token-v2.redwood.net (we've seen some customers still reference legacy hostnames which change routing). Also, can you provide a short sample of the client request IDs (transaction id or client-side UUID) so we can cross-reference with our traces?

We'll compile a timeline and a proposed window during the afternoon and share the telemetry bundle. If the window is confirmed, we'll also propose a proportional credit calculation and schedule a postmortem.

Sincerely,
Rachel Kim
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Rachel —

SC-REQ-20271102-9932, c3f1a4b8-9a2d-4f6a-a9d7
SC-REQ-20271102-9967, 4b7f2f1c-e6d3-4458-97f1
SC-REQ-20271102-9981, 6cc2b2a0-1fd7-49b9-8f4e

We were definitely pointing at token-v2.redwood.net (same as our previous calls). We've attached a short snippet of the client retry logic and the bulk traces folder (link in attachment) — you should see the retry amplification pattern: backoff didn't kick in fast enough because client treats 5xx as transient and immediately requeues.

We'd like Redwood to: 1) verify the exact unavailable window; 2) confirm whether this qualifies for SLA credit; 3) schedule a joint postmortem (include your infra and release leads).

Also: our legal team asked we include the signed SLA (attachment) in the thread for reference.

—Aisha
attachments: silvercart-raw-traces-20271102.tar.gz, sla-signed-v2.pdf

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@silvercart.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 16:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: High retry volume after token endpoint 503s (observed 03:12–03:35 UTC)

Hi Aisha —

Thank you for the sample IDs and the traces. We've completed a preliminary cross-check:
- Confirmed that between 2027-11-02T03:12:10Z and 2027-11-02T03:34:50Z there was a cluster-level control-plane handoff in us-west-2 that caused a short period where token-v2 service returned 503s for a subset of shards.
- Root cause (prelim): an autoscaler race condition combined with a cascading KV-cache warmup that briefly left routing tables inconsistent during failover.

Based on the SLA definitions in your signed contract (SLA v2, section 4.1), we believe this meets the threshold for "severe degradation" for the affected region and will propose a proportional credit. We'll calculate the pro-rata credit based on impacted token request volume and share the math in a follow-up email.

Next steps I'd like to propose:
1) Postmortem call with engineering and ops on Thu Nov 4 at 15:00 UTC (60 minutes). Please confirm attendee list.
2) We'll provide a full evidence bundle including our raw traces, the shard-level error histograms, and the remediation timeline by EOD Wed.
3) Draft credit calculation (preliminary) attached as a short spreadsheet link — we'll finalize with you once you confirm the impacted request volume.

Cc'ing Soojin (Release Engineering) and David (SRE) so they can join the postmortem and own remediation items.

Apologies for the customer impact — we'll make the remediation and a long-term control fix a priority in the coming sprint.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
attachments: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-silvercart-traces
